standard_prerequisites.name: The internal hom of derived quasi-coherent objects with the stated hypotheses lands in D_QCoh, so the assertion is local on X
On affines the evaluate map is an isomorphism in the module setting under the corresponding boundedness hypotheses
On affines pseudo-coherence, perfectness, and finite tor dimension of objects agree with the corresponding module properties
Locally a perfect object is a finite complex of finite free modules, for which the evaluate map is visibly an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Treats case (2) without quasi-coherence of either side.

core_obligations: Cases (1) and (3): by the quasi-coherence internal-hom lemma the question is local on X; on affines the module-level evaluate map is an isomorphism by the More on Algebra lemma, using the affine pseudo-coherence, perfectness, and tor-dimension lemmas to translate the hypotheses (proof lines 2738-2744).

Case (2): neither side need be in D_QCoh, but the assertion is local; locally K is a finite complex of finite free modules, and for such K the evaluate map K ⊗ R\SheafHom(M, L) → R\SheafHom(M, K ⊗ L) is an isomorphism directly (proof lines 2745-2749).
proof_roadmap: Reduce cases (1) and (3) to the affine module statement and translate the hypotheses (proof lines 2738-2744).
Handle case (2) by a local reduction to finite free complexes (proof lines 2745-2749).
